prompt: Create a new SOLIDWORKS part: a centred 100 x 60 x 10 mm rectangular plate with one centred 20 mm diameter Through All hole. Rebuild and save as phone-tests/Plate-001.sldprt inside the configured workspace, without overwriting. Leave existing documents untouched.

plan.Summary: Proposed creation of a new SOLIDWORKS part containing a centred 100 mm × 60 mm rectangular plate, extruded 10 mm in one direction from the Top Plane along its default positive normal, with a centred 20 mm diameter Through All cut made from a second Top Plane sketch. Rebuild and save to the configured workspace at phone-tests/Plate-001.sldprt without overwriting or modifying existing documents.
Assumptions: The configured workspace root is already known to the CAD execution environment.
The save operation may create the missing phone-tests subfolder within the configured workspace, as explicitly authorized.
Creating a new part does not close, save, or modify any currently open documents.
Sketch coordinates are in millimetres, with the rectangle centred at the Top Plane sketch origin and aligned so 100 mm lies along sketch X and 60 mm lies along sketch Y.
The default positive normal direction for a one-direction extrusion from the Top Plane is used.

revisions.prompt: Create a new SOLIDWORKS part: a centred 100 x 60 x 10 mm rectangular plate with one centred 20 mm diameter Through All hole. Rebuild and save as phone-tests/Plate-001.sldprt inside the configured workspace, without overwriting. Leave existing documents untouched.

interpretation.Summary: Create a new SOLIDWORKS part containing a 100 mm × 60 mm rectangular plate, centred at the origin on the Top Plane, extruded to 10 mm thickness. Add a 20 mm diameter hole centred at the origin and cut it Through All. Rebuild and save as phone-tests/Plate-001.sldprt within the configured workspace without overwriting. Keep all pre-existing documents open and unchanged.
Assumptions: The plate's 100 mm × 60 mm footprint is centred at the origin, with the 100 mm dimension along sketch X and the 60 mm dimension along sketch Y.

Because the command protocol does not provide a mid-plane extrusion option, the 10 mm thickness is extruded in the default positive normal direction from the Top Plane rather than centred about that plane.
The centred hole means its axis passes through the plate centre at sketch coordinates (0 mm, 0 mm).
The relative save path is resolved inside the configured workspace, and the phone-tests directory already exists or is handled by the CAD environment.
No existing document will be closed, saved, activated for modification, or otherwise altered; a separate new part will be created.
Ambiguities: The request does not specify whether the 10 mm thickness must be symmetric about the Top Plane; the available protocol supports only a one-direction 10 mm extrusion.
The request does not specify the extrusion direction relative to the Top Plane; the CAD system's default positive normal direction will be used.
The request does not state whether missing folders should be created automatically; the plan assumes the configured workspace can resolve the requested relative path.
